tagline: Up Tunkhannock Creek, under one great viaduct and on to another.
intro: At Dixon, PA 92 leaves US 6 and heads north along the Tunkhannock Creek through woods and farm fields, by East Lemon and Starkville, to Nicholson. From there it runs on through Lenox, South Gibson and Jackson to Susquehanna Depot on the North Branch of the Susquehanna, and the byway ends at Lanesboro, some 37 miles of valley farmland and bluestone quarry country.
Nicholson drew national attention in the last week of July 1986, when an escaped Bengal tiger was hunted for several days around the area. It was never found.

moments.title: Tunkhannock Viaduct
moments.text: In Nicholson the road passes beneath the 1915 railroad viaduct, 240 feet above the creek, the largest concrete structure in the world when it was finished and still in daily freight service.

moments.title: Susquehanna Depot
moments.text: The Erie's shops here grew to more than 1,000 workers and a 33-stall roundhouse, and by 1887 they were turning out five locomotives a month.

moments.title: Starrucca Viaduct
moments.text: Near Lanesboro the Erie's bluestone arches have carried trains over Starrucca Creek since 1848, when this was the largest stone railway viaduct in the world.
